Day 3. In the Monday meeting, Suraj said, "Some of us actually read the spec." Everyone heard it. Pradeep studied his notes and, wanting to avoid awkwardness, moved on to the next item.

Day 17. The comments in meetings got sharper. Two developers now ate lunch with Suraj, while the other three sat at the far table.

Day 34. Farhan, the target of most of the remarks, had a calendar entry marked "personal" on Wednesday afternoon. Pradeep guessed it was an interview. He asked in the last meeting, "Is everything okay with the team?" Nobody answered.

qa.q: What did Suraj say in the Monday meeting?
qa.a: Suraj said, "Some of us actually read the spec."

qa.q: Why did Pradeep move on to the next item?
qa.a: Pradeep wanted to avoid awkwardness, so he ignored the sharp comment and hoped the tension would fade.

qa.q: What could Pradeep have done on Day 3, and why?
qa.a: Pradeep could have spoken to Suraj privately that day about the remark, because a small talk early is easier than a divided team later.

qa.q: How might Farhan have felt as the remarks continued?
qa.a: Farhan probably felt targeted and unsupported, which may be why Farhan started looking for another job.

passage:
Gopika, you're asking whether to say something about those two in your team? Let me, your Sangeeta aunty, tell you what I did at the bank branch in my thirties.
Two of my clerks, Philomena and Harpreet, began making little digs at each other in the morning meeting. "Some people finish their work on time." That kind of thing. I hated awkward talks, so I laughed it off and moved to the next point. Surely it would fade, I thought.
It didn't. Within two months, the cashiers took Philomena's side and the loan desk took Harpreet's. Lunch became two separate tables. And one day Harpreet handed me a letter: she had applied to another branch.
I remember sitting in my cabin feeling foolish. She was one of my best people.
So, my girl, the silence you think is kindness can spread. Talk to them early.

qa.a: Harpreet handed her a letter saying she had applied to another branch.

qa.q: How did Sangeeta feel sitting in the cabin after Harpreet's letter?
qa.a: She felt foolish and regretful, because her hope that the digs would fade had cost her one of her best people.

qa.q: Where was the turning point in the story, and what could Sangeeta have done differently there?
qa.a: The turning point was the first morning meeting with the digs; instead of laughing it off, she could have spoken to both clerks privately or set a clear rule for the meetings.

qa.q: How did the silence affect Philomena and Harpreet's colleagues?
qa.a: The cashiers and the loan desk were pulled into taking sides, so ordinary lunch breaks split into two separate tables and the whole branch felt tense.

grounding: It shows an elder recalling how ignoring sharp comments to avoid awkwardness let the tension spread, made others take sides and pushed one member to look for another job.

The monsoon had flooded the ground floor of the design studio, so the whole team was squeezed around one table upstairs, laptops balanced on boxes.
Uma, the studio lead, heard Damini mutter, "Must be nice to leave at five," as Kirti packed up. Kirti's jaw tightened. Uma looked down at her screen. With the flood repairs and the deadline, she had no energy for a scene. It'll blow over, she told herself.
It didn't. Over the next weeks the cramped room made every remark louder. The juniors began eating lunch with whichever of the two they liked. Someone left a sticky note on Kirti's chair: "Team player?"
When the ground floor finally reopened, Kirti asked Uma for a reference letter. "I've got an interview in Chennai," she said, not meeting her eyes.
Uma sat alone at the long table, the smell of damp still in the carpet.

qa.q: Why was the whole team squeezed around one table upstairs?
qa.a: The monsoon had flooded the ground floor of the design studio.

qa.q: Why did Uma look down at her screen when Damini made the remark?
qa.a: Uma was tired and anxious to avoid an awkward scene, with the flood repairs and the deadline already weighing on her, so she hoped the comment would blow over.

qa.q: What would you change first in Uma's approach?
qa.a: Speak to Damini and Kirti soon after the first sharp remark, perhaps separately, instead of hoping the tension fades on its own.

qa.q: What is it like for Kirti when Uma says nothing?
qa.a: Kirti is left to face the remarks and the sticky note alone, and she likely feels unsupported and isolated enough to look for another job.

grounding: It shows a lead ignoring sharp comments to avoid awkwardness, while the tension spreads, others pick sides and one member starts looking for another job.
